Writing them found a real porting gap - computeFlashBlackOil's ~disgas branch was omitted entirely, so a disgas=False/vapoil=True model reported hydrocarbon status 1 where MRST reports 3 - and two facts about findHAP that its control had to be rebuilt around: neither diagonal anisotropy nor a uniform off-diagonal tensor moves an interior harmonic averaging point off its face centroid; only heterogeneity does. The transport Jacobian matches central differences of its own residual to 5.3e-10 relative, and that check turned out to bound what such a comparison can prove: swapping the upwind side changes residual and Jacobian consistently and every finite-difference test still passed, so flow direction, source sign and the fractional-flow weighting of production are asserted directly. | compute_gradient_adjoint_ad (7 tests, tests/optimization/test_compute_gradient_adjoint_ad.py). The adjoint is checked against a central finite difference of the objective for every control of every step, and that comparison is stronger here than the transport-Jacobian one it resembles: there, residual and Jacobian shared a formulation so a consistent error moved both, while here the finite difference re-runs the full nonlinear forward simulation and the adjoint uses transposed Jacobians in a backward sweep. 9 mutations, all caught - both transposes dropped, the backward time coupling dropped, the objective-derivative sign flipped, the sweep run forwards, supplied states ignored, a 0.1% drift between the two copies, and a copy given its own result type. | es_mda (9 tests, tests/ensemble/test_es_mda.py). The defect this module invites is a mismatch between two numbers that must agree: observations are perturbed with noise scaled by sqrt(alpha) while the update inflates the observation covariance by alpha, so scaling the noise by alpha instead gives perturbed data with covariance alpha^2*R against an update assuming alpha*R - the run still completes and the misfit still falls. es_mda takes its generator as an argument, so with a stub returning all-ones noise the whole four-step assimilation is replayed by hand through enkf_update and compared at atol=0. 9 mutations, all caught: noise scaled by alpha, the alpha*R inflation dropped, R used in place of its Cholesky factor, no re-simulation between assimilations, the sum(1/alpha)=1 constraint disabled, esmda_alphas returning ones, the misfit history reduced to its final entry, and an in-place optimisation writing through to the caller's prior. | get_initialization_regions_deck (10 tests, tests/ad_core/test_get_initialization_regions_deck.py). This one partitions the grid, and a partition has two properties worth more than any tolerance: every cell in exactly one region, no cell in none. A cell in two is equilibrated twice and keeps whichever scatter came last; a cell in none keeps whatever it was initialised to; neither raises. The active-cell trap is the same shape as the ECLIPSE reader's - REGIONS arrays are written over the Cartesian box - so the indexMap path is tested on a grid that actually has inactive cells, since a Cartesian grid cannot exercise it. 10 mutations, all caught after correcting two of my own: indexMap ignored, SATNUM and PVTNUM each dropped from the subregion filter, the gas-oil and oil-water contacts swapped, the capillary contacts swapped, OWC read from the GOC column, every region's datum taken from the first EQUIL record, and a fluid with no surface densities accepted. | The last three numerical modules on the risk list, closing it. re_mpfa newton_solver (10 tests, tests/re_mpfa/test_newton_solver.py): a linear residual must converge in exactly two iterations - not about two - and the modified-Picard argument contract is watched rather than assumed, since h_n0 and previous coincide on the first iteration and swapping them yields a solver that still converges, to a different time discretisation. ml/tensors (10 tests): the module's own docstring claims float64 by default to preserve MRST parity, so that is asserted, along with connectivity staying int64 when float32 is requested - indices are identity, not measurement, and past 2^24 cells a float32 index stops being exact. ml/datasets (14 tests): item i must pair step i with step i+1, asserted against values that encode their own step, because a dataset returning the identity map trains happily and nothing downstream notices. 28 mutations across the three, all caught after correcting two fixtures of my own.

blockers: 13 of the 19 still have no focused test. The detector has been corrected twice and both times it was over-reporting: matching dotted paths alone claimed 165 modules and 25k lines, wrongly including research_studio files whose tests import them through the package; requiring a *unique* symbol then still missed the re-export pattern and listed simulate_packed_problem, which has 12 dedicated tests. Coverage is now credited for a dotted path, a unique public symbol, or a package path together with the module basename. Ranking the remaining 19 modules surfaced a porting defect rather than a coverage gap: diagnostics/utils/compute_time_of_flight.py, compute_tof_and_tracer.py and compute_well_pairs.py are byte-identical apart from two docstring lines, and all three define the same Diagnostics/compute_diagnostics pair. They name three distinct MRST functions - computeTimeOfFlight returns [T, A, q], computeTOFandTracer returns D, computeWellPairs takes (state, G, rock, W, D) and returns WP - so at most one of the three is a port and the other two are unported. Only compute_time_of_flight is imported (by utils/__init__); the other two are unreferenced. Separately, that file duplicates rather than re-exports flow_diagnostics.compute_diagnostics, so pymrst.modules.diagnostics.Diagnostics is not pymrst.modules.diagnostics.utils.Diagnostics despite identical fields - an isinstance trap. Writing tests against these three would have certified the duplication instead of finding it. No diagnostics parity ledger exists, which is how this went unrecorded. Needs an owner decision: port the two missing functions, or collapse the copies. | A SECOND duplication, of the same family as the diagnostics trio but milder, found while closing this gap: optimization/utils/compute_gradient_adjoint_ad.py re-implements the backward sweep already in optimization/adjoint.py, the bodies differing only in a docstring, one comment and line wrapping. The MRST-homing shim under ad_core/simulators/ correctly re-exports instead, so pymrst.modules.optimization.compute_gradient_adjoint and the function at the MRST path are different objects. Unlike the diagnostics trio there is no isinstance trap - both import AdjointResult from one place - and the two agree numerically today. Deduplicating is a change to the replica layer rather than an addition to it, so it is left as an owner decision and the drift is pinned by a test that fails the day one copy is fixed without the other. The 6 numerical modules on the risk list are now all covered. One claim was checked and withdrawn rather than asserted: for a linear-Gaussian problem ES-MDA's tempered updates are often said to compose to a single update, which holds for the exact Kalman recursion but not for this deterministic per-realization form, whose anomalies transform as (I-KG)A and shrink faster than the Kalman covariance - measured, one assimilation and four differ by 0.30 in posterior mean. Asserting the identity would have pinned a false claim. | Two small defects recorded rather than repaired, both because changing them alters behaviour callers can already observe. get_initialization_regions_deck's _phase_densities(model, pvt_region) accepts the region and never reads it, so a deck whose PVT regions carry different DENSITY records initialises every region from the same surface densities; whether MRST looks these up per region is not verifiable here, as there is no MATLAB source in this tree, so the test pins the behaviour that exists rather than one claimed for MRST. And its ValueError('deck SOLUTION.EQUIL is required') is unreachable for an ABSENT EQUIL - _section returns {} and np.asarray({}, dtype=float) raises TypeError first - so the common case gets an opaque message; an empty EQUIL does reach the guard. Two tests in this file were also found to pass for weaker reasons than intended and say so in their docstrings: the partition test needed PVTNUM to vary before it could detect PVTNUM being ignored, and the empty-region check pins an outcome that a redundant guard and an empty pairs array both produce. | Four tests across these three files pass for weaker or narrower reasons than their names suggest, and each says so in its own docstring rather than being left to look like protection it does not give: newton_solver's symmetric test operator made a transposed-solve defect undetectable until the operator was made non-symmetric; dropping .copy() on h_n0 is inert because h_ad.val is rebound rather than mutated, so the falsifying mutation is moving the assignment into the loop; the dataset's positive-side bounds check is redundant with numpy's own, while the negative side is load-bearing - without it ds[-9] silently returns a real-looking pair from the wrong end; and the npz .copy() is redundant today, kept as a guard for the day mmap_mode is added.

numerical_validation: measured across four model families: 9.89e-17 (SPE1 PseudoOil/PseudoGas), 1.74e-16 (water, fully coupled), 9.72e-08 (Norne mini oil-water poromechanics) and 4.17e-06 (water, fixed-stress). The three fully implicit cases conserve at or near machine precision. The fixed-stress figure is unexplained and its cause has been asserted twice and refuted twice - see blockers. Norne's water component carries its check: injection drives the inventory from 0 to 160,000 surface m3 and 50,000 m3 per step balances to about 0.015. Verified by perturbation - a 1e-06 error in sW yields a 1e-06 imbalance, a flipped well sign yields 2.0.
performance_evidence: scripts/freeze_characterization.py --perf measures section 16's observe-profile overhead directly, because the session evaluates the invariant suite and the conservation adapter once per accepted state - they are on the critical path, not beside it. Marginal cost over the same session with its store: -1% on the 42 ms case and +1% on Norne's 7.2 s run, both inside the measurement spread. Verified by sleeping 5 ms per invariant evaluation, which moves the reading to +38%. Measured against the store-session baseline rather than the bare solve: against the bare solve the profile read cheaper than the store alone, which is a strict subset of it.
blockers: one number is unexplained: 4.17e-06 on fixed-stress water, against machine precision on every fully implicit case. Characterized rather than explained, which is the useful handoff. The raw imbalance is a constant RATE - 2.895e-09 m3/s, identical across steps of different length - and is about 0.25 of the well rate. That fraction is stable under grid refinement (0.2463 to 0.2509 for nx in 10-40 and ny in 2-8) and under fluid and rock compressibility (0.2222 to 0.2673 while c_fluid/c_rock spans 0.125 to 0.75). So a roughly fixed quarter of injected volume does not reach the inventory, and it is not a discretization artifact. Two tempting readings of the quarter are already ruled out: it is not 1/ny (unchanged at ny=2 and ny=8) and not c_fluid/c_rock (unchanged while that ratio varies sixfold). Five causes tested and refuted: poromechanical coupling (it was WaterConservationAdapter silently using b=1 on a PhaseFluid with no b_w; taking b from the state-function graph moved the fully coupled case from 5.25e-07 to 1.74e-16); operator splitting (splitting_tol across six orders, unmoved); Newton tolerances tol_mb and tol_cnv (no response); the post-convergence mechanics re-solve in FixedStressWaterWellModel (removing it changes nothing); and FixedStressPoreVolume read with the wrong fixed_stress terms (recomputing each state with the terms in force when it was accepted gives the identical number). Two of those were written into this ledger as fact before being tested; no further guess belongs here without an experiment behind it.
acceptance_decision: not accepted: a budget is owed and cannot be set responsibly yet. Three of four families conserve at or near machine precision; the fourth sits at 4.17e-06 for reasons not established, and a budget drawn above it would be a number chosen to pass rather than a bound anyone can defend.

Active-cell mapping is the load-bearing part and is tested on a grid that actually has inactive cells - Norne mini has none, so it cannot exercise it: a Cartesian-length PERMX maps onto exactly the active indices while an active-length PORO passes through, and a length matching neither is refused by name. read_eclipse_case uses split_disconnected=False deliberately, because PyMRST's default returns a list of components and keeping one would silently drop part of the model; the disconnection is reported by inspection.validate instead. keyword_support() states what is read, ignored, refused and not implemented. | The keyword coverage report the package asks for is now built, in eclipse/coverage.py. keyword_support() says what the reader understands in general; this answers the narrower and more useful question - for THIS file, what gets used and what gets dropped - which matters because read_eclipse_case is permissive by design and a case built from a file full of unrecognised keywords loads cleanly while quietly not being the case on disk. integration_evidence: validate(grid, rock, wells) returns ordered findings; explain_connection(a, b) names the shared faces with areas and optional transmissibilities, or gives a reason rather than a bare negative; inspect_cell(i) reports geometry, neighbours and properties. Transmissibility and fault findings added: face_transmissibility harmonic-averages the half-face values compute_trans returns, and sealed faces are kept at exactly zero rather than a numerical floor, because a floor makes a deliberate seal indistinguishable from an anomalously small face. On Norne mini validate() now reports two INFO lines - 221 fault faces, 493 sealed interior faces - and zero warnings. | Twisted cells and face orientation complete the required list, in inspection/geometry.py. A twisted cell is compute_trans with the permeability removed - the cell centroid on the wrong side of its own face - so the check names the same cells the negative half-transmissibilities land in, which is asserted rather than assumed. The port's MRST-faithful fix_negative=True default replaces those with abs() and warns to stderr, so the defect is repaired before the user sees anything; a test asserts that identity (2 of 110 negative on a spiked corner-point cell, returned array exactly abs(raw)) so the justification cannot quietly stop being true. Reversed face normals are a separate ERROR: nothing crashes, flow through the face runs backwards. Writing this exposed a third defect class - a grid whose cells.faces and faces.neighbors disagree makes compute_trans flip the normal silently - which is now checked first, with the geometry checks declining to run rather than misreporting an inconsistency as a twist. 6 mutations, all caught.
